newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan court passes first drug death sentence.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan court passes first drug death sentence.

text.p: A Pakistani court in the Punjab province capital of Lahore handed down the country's first death sentence against a drug trafficker on Tuesday, state television said.

It said Additional Sessions Judge (Narcotics) Chaudhry Liaquat Ali sentenced the driver of a taxi rickshaw, Manzoor Ahmad, to death and ordered him to pay a fine of one million rupees ($24,734) for carrying 37.5 kg (82.67 lbs) of hashish in 1995.
Ahmad has the right to appeal against the sentence to a higher court.

It was the first time a Pakistani court has condemned a drug smuggler to death since parliament passed a law in 1994 raising the maximum sentence for drugs offences to death from 25 years' hard labour in prison, legal sources said.
